$comment: Read from the SIA chart set AD 2 LFDI (AIP France, chart dated 2025-02-20): the reporting points come from the coordinates table of the chart,
the notes from the English column of its text pages, both read by a script and checked (each point lies within 80 NM of the aerodrome).
Only what the chart prints is recorded; nothing is deduced. Services, frequencies, elevation, position, magnetic variation and runways
were first extracted automatically from the chart text. Drawings (circuit, routes, radials) are not read.
The charts themselves are (c) SIA and are not redistributed. Flight simulation only: never use for real navigation.
name: Libourne - Artigues-de-Lussac

source.extraction: chart text, table and English column read by script, checked

preferredQfuReason: preferred QFU 215, due to noise pollution
notes: AD reserved for radio-equipped ACFT.
TWY A: paved TWY principal (width: 7.5 m)
TWY B: paved TWY (width: 5 m).
TWY C: grass TWY.
Simultaneous use of RWY prohibited.
Simultaneous use of RWY or TWY and HEL TWY (translation by ground effect) prohibited.
Unpaved RWY reserved for home-based and ultra light ACFT.
Unpaved RWY and TWY cannot be used during rainy weather.
Business aviation or parking for more than 2 HR on paved apron: O/R PN 24 HR by TEL operator.
Taxiing prohibited except on RWY and TWY.
Preferred QFU 215° due to noise pollution.
Low altitude circuit patterns (700 ft AMSL MNM) for training flights by day only with an instructor on board.
Take-off RWY 04 day or night: climb MAG 045° up to 700 ft AMSL due to noise pollution.
In case of North/North-West wind, heavy turbulence and windshears may occur on both QFU.
Approved with limitations (because the power supply is not backed up): 1- for home-based pilots, after having passed a practical night flight aptitude exam on site with a qualified instructor.

2- for non home-based pilots: Have a minimum experience of 200 hours of flight including 20 hours at night and recent practice (3 takeoffs and 3 landings at night in the last 3 months) or have passed a practical flight aptitude exam at night on site with a qualified instructor.
Pilots must contact the aerodrome operator with PPR PN 48 HR by the means of communication mentioned on the aeronautical chart.
Only taxiway A can be used at night.
PCL coupled with PAPIs on A/A FREQ.
AEM (NR 9145): SR-SS, 330 ft ASFC MAX.
As per protocol.
Aerobatics activity on AD (NR 6606): SR-SS; 1000 m along RWY 04/22 axis, centered on ARP; 1700 ft AMSL / 2700 ft AMSL.
Activity announced on A/A FREQ.
